subject: Mutual action plan & champion brief for CloudRidge evaluation
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Evan Clarke <evan.clarke@cloudridge.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@cloudridge.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 4 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + immediate next steps

Hi Evan / Maya —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

What we heard (your team)
- Primary use case: real-time summarization + internal knowledge retrieval for support agents (low-latency, high-throughput).
- Success metrics: 75% reduction in handle time on tier-1 tickets; <150ms incremental generation latency for the fast path.
- Security must-haves: private VPC deployment or dedicated tenancy, audit logs for session-level retention controls.

Immediate asks from your side
1) Confirm the economic buyer — you mentioned Maya and the Head of Ops might be final approver. Can you share name/email?
2) Procurement timeline & required docs — any standard questionnaire or PO process we should start preparing for?
3) Champion readiness — who will be the internal advocate on day-to-day adoption and enablement?

Our proposal:
- I’ll share a 1-page mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones and owners today.
- Security snapshot and deployment options attached for procurement review.
- Schedule 30-min commercial/finance sync next week to cover pricing bands and reserved capacity (if you want predictable throughput).

Next call slots: Tue 5/5 10–11am PT, Wed 5/6 2–3pm PT — tell me what works and I’ll send the invite.

Attachments: CloudRidge-MAP-v1.xlsx, redwood-security-snapshot.pdf

Thanks — Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

From: Evan Clarke <evan.clarke@cloudridge.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@cloudridge.com>, procure@cloudridge.com
Date: Mon, 4 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + immediate next steps

Thanks Priya — great demo and tidy recap. Quick answers inline:  

Economic buyer:
- Final approver will be Tomas Alvarez (CFO) — tomas.alvarez@cloudridge.com (I’ll intro him once we have a MAP and a rough order value).

Procurement & required docs:
- Standard vendor security questionnaire + our vendor onboarding packet. I attached a redacted one here (procurement included on cc). Our procurement lead expects a SOC2 report and the security snapshot you attached should speed review.
- Typical procurement timeline is 3–6 weeks post-MAP if legal redlines are minimal.

Champion:
- Maya will be the product champion and lead the POC. She’ll own the internal pilot and success metrics.

Decision criteria (from internal stakeholders):
- Cost per 1k tokens under production load, predictable throughput for business hours, audit/retention controls, and SLA for uptime.

I’ll accept 5/5 10:30am PT for the commercial sync. Please include a one-pager with reserve vs burst cost assumptions.

—Evan
Evan Clarke
Director of Product Operations | CloudRidge

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 4 May 2027 12:02:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: CloudRidge champion arming & MAP draft (please review)

Team —

Captured outcomes from the demo with CloudRidge (see Evan’s reply). They’ve named Maya as the product champion and Tomas (CFO) as the economic buyer. Procurement loop included. I’ve attached the first MAP draft (CloudRidge-MAP-v1.xlsx) and the security snapshot.

What I need from you: 
- Aditya: build a 1-slide pricing range that shows Reserved (Dedicated) vs Hosted per-month economics at projected pilot volume (we should show sensitivity to tokens/day). Highlight path to predictable unit cost.
- Neha: pre-draft a short security FAQ (2–3 bullets) focused on SOC2, logging/retention options, and KMS integration — something Maya can send to procurement immediately.
- Tessa: recommend 3 internal enablement assets for Maya (talk track bullets, 5-slide pilot kit, and an ROI one-pager). Keep language concise and non-technical for exec review.

Champion talk-track bullets for Maya (raw — feel free to edit):
- Problem statement: Our support agents waste time switching systems and searching context; Redwood reduces average handle time by surfacing the right context in-line.
- Pilot ask: 4-week pilot focused on tier-1 volume with scripted success criteria (25–30% reduction in handle time).
- Exec pitch for Tomas: predictable per-ticket cost, ability to reserve capacity for peak hours, and compliance controls — we’ll provide a modeled TCO vs current tooling.

Timing: please return slides/docs by Tue 5/5 3pm PT so I can package before the 5/5 commercial sync.

Thanks — Priya
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 4 May 2027 13:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: CloudRidge champion arming & MAP draft (please review)

Nice note — I’ll do the pricing slide. One tweak to the exec pitch: explicitly call out a 12-month reserved commit scenario and include a worst/best case on token growth (conservative +30%/optimistic +90%). Also suggest we include an optional SLA credit schedule (e.g., 99.5% uptime credit) to show enterprise readiness.

Aditya
Account Director | Redwood Inference

Following up with the MAP attached (CloudRidge-MAP-v1.xlsx) and a short security FAQ (redwood-security-snapshot.pdf). Per Evan’s ask, I included a pricing slide that shows Reserved vs Hosted bands and a conservative token growth scenario. Aditya and Neha helped with the materials — cc’d.

Immediate next steps: 
- Commercial sync (30m): Tue 5/11 10:30–11:00am PT — invite sent.

- Exec intro to Tomas: Evan, if you can introduce Tomas after the commercial sync that would be perfect — we’ll include the MAP and the modeled TCO in that note.
